# PROGRAM result sizing: final proposed effective-contract amendment

**Fixed audit ID: `program-result-sizing-r94-v1`. Status: proposed; inactive.** This complete body consolidates the accepted design and its two low-severity precision notes. It becomes normative only after the original peer identifies and dispositions these exact frozen bytes and Root explicitly adopts them in R94. Acceptance of the earlier design is not adoption of this final body. Until that adoption, the existing result/reservation limits remain in force; the separate R93 writer must not implement this amendment.

The immutable inputs are [the design](task-6-result-size-design.md), 31,338 bytes / `f20c5e61c778d52f82419b9a67da7aae6eed908a3d5a38c2ebe89bffd65d963d`, and [the full independent review](task-6-result-size-design-independent-review.md), 18,837 bytes / `48febfacbe8e0f4e50abf14f14511d1a8ca375c87c38fae51009005b4dc8c390`. Both remain unchanged. Their source observations and sizing examples below are historical evidence, not fresh observations of the concurrently changing R93 implementation. This body contains no own length/hash field and no future K/A/I/L identity.

**Normative proposed rule, conditional on activation above:** permit at most **262,144 UTF-8 bytes, including the final LF**, for the full, uncompressed local PROGRAM result original. In the same authenticated R90 PROGRAM scope, permit at most **458,752 bytes of combined positive outer reservation**: one result of at most 262,144 plus at most **196,608 bytes of all other chargeable outer originals**. Keep the existing scalar `plans.outerReserveBytes` and budget fields; enforce both the combined bound and the independent non-result bound. A change to the writer and reader constants alone is insufficient.

These are allocations **inside** R90's unchanged whole-invocation normal numeric and normal aggregate allowances. They supply no extra numeric, aggregate, bootstrap, runtime, source-file, native132, Engine or retrieval capacity. Retain full JSON and every fact. Do not add a format, sharding protocol, role registry, retry, test flag or candidate-selectable bypass. Root owns the subsequent R94 disposition, coordinated implementation-plan amendment and implementation dispatch after the separate R93 task review. This document authorizes no source edit or operation.

## Evidence and the actual obstruction

The accepted design and peer independently read and hashed the complete immutable [result original](task-6-clock-purity-checkpoint-30/full-canary-result-original.json): **231,064 bytes**, SHA-256 `7ec5f7bc03277469fe4054d56695a14c8929cc780e236e3a5e3cbebe8e99882e`. The [exact JS layout](task-6-clock-purity-checkpoint-30/full-canary-result-layout.json) is 4,384 bytes, SHA-256 `8882e827811e336eb0de32d53db8b7bdf936d617bfe502275f3e3100a73c439b`. Its record is 90,130 bytes, observation 136,312, and remaining values, property names, punctuation and LF 4,622. It contains all 64 episodes. It exceeds 196,608 by **34,456** and leaves **31,080** below the proposed result maximum.

This is SIMULATED unchanged-train evidence through real private replay/effects code. It establishes a serialized size, not native/media, current-image, clock, outer-admission or actual-fit approval. The original design read the then-current fix3 brief, implementation report and R87/R90/R91 originals; its source observations were made while checkpoint30 repairs were moving. Those historical observations are retained here without reinterpreting the current source or its timing. The unchanged witness remains a negative under its old result and reservation limits.

Three independent gates matter:

1. `artifacts.mjs:98` writes the result at 196,608 and requires it to fit the remaining outer reservation.
2. `event-marker-native-controller.mjs:111` independently reads the exact result original at 196,608, then compares its entire bytes with `JSON.stringify(serialized) + LF`.
3. `event-marker-program-guards.mjs:52` caps **the whole** `plans.outerReserveBytes` at 196,608. `codec-record.mjs:32` reserves it before observation/replay. Thus even a larger per-file writer cannot fund this result, much less its receipt and outer documents.

The third gate is an explicit additional change proposed for R94. It must not be presented as an interpretation of the old all-caps-unchanged instructions.

## Informative alternatives retained from the accepted design

Only approach A is specified by this proposed amendment. These comparisons preserve the accepted rationale; they do not authorize another representation, sharding path or fallback policy.

| Option | Concrete outcome and cost | Disposition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **A. Full JSON, bounded result and combined reservation** | Witness stays exactly 231,064 bytes. No fact transformation or decoding layer. Requires coordinated writer, private-scope selection, independent outer reader, reservation and result-loading checks. Worst result-original increase over the old per-document ceiling is 65,536 bytes per actual copy. | **Selected approach**, with 262,144 result / 196,608 other outer / 458,752 combined bounds and all existing total charges. |
| **B. Existing episode wire plus explicit residual fields** | The 185-byte existing episode leaf is 248 Base64 characters; 64 leaves alone occupy 16,065 JSON bytes instead of the current 80,632-byte episode array. However, this result also has `firstEnd`, `lastStart` and `id`; the ordinary `unpackAudioEpisode` view does not preserve all three by itself. A sizing-only container `{schema:"marker-wire-episode-v2",leaves:[...],firstEndLastStart:[[...],...]}` is 16,830 bytes on this witness, giving a **167,262-byte** result and **29,346-byte** headroom under 196,608. IDs can be implicit only after proving each is exactly its row index. | Viable fallback if A is rejected, but this is **not** an implemented or round-trip-verified encoding. It needs exact field closure, all fact mutations, pre-expansion bounds and complete consumer migration. The old combined 196,608 reservation would leave only 29,346 for every other outer original, so compacting the result alone still does not establish end-to-end fit. |
| **B, shared fields only** | Even deleting the two duplicate assurance values, one duplicate clock value and observation visual value would save only about 10,078 value bytes before reference overhead. That does not cover the 34,456-byte excess. | Insufficient alone; no need for a new general deduplication scheme. |
| **C. References/shards** | A reference does not possess its original. All members, inventories, hashes, every actual use, reconstruction and retained copies must remain bounded and charged. Splitting 231,064 logical bytes into smaller objects does not satisfy an unchanged 196,608 logical-result limit; adopting the larger logical limit removes the reason to shard this witness. Additional members also consume the existing 257-object allowance. | Do not use here. No hash-only possession, per-shard cap reset or dropped reference/detector facts. |

For B, preserve all other result fields, raw endpoints, prelude ownership/counts, guard facts, residual scan totals and independent comparisons. Require exact decoded equality to the original logical object, including extra/missing fields, before treating it as lossless. Packing a partial projection and silently regenerating the rest is insufficient. No code or data charge changes follow from encoding.

## Scope, consumers and interfaces

Use the existing evidence-policy module for the few fixed limits and scope predicate. The larger result allowance requires the private acquired `trustedStackMeasurement` dependencies, matching R90 profile/plans/intent policy, owned mass invocation, and authenticated `execution.domain=program`, `producer=root-program-v1`, `retrieval=root-originals-v1` with the existing workload command checks. The public frontdoor still selects its exact unchanged canary invocation. A policy ID, filename, role, environment class, supplied result flag or larger `plans.outerReserveBytes` alone cannot select it. Native132 shares R90's numeric policy but does **not** get this allowance.

Keep `plans.outerReserveBytes` as the **combined** requested allowance, now bounded by 458,752 only in that scope. The reviewed plan can request the maximum so the result can use its full cap. Legacy/sourceClosed/unselected/native132 retain their existing reservation ceiling. Bind the actual plan bytes through the existing manifest/K/profile/intent review and private acquisition. Its schema and reservation field remain; the effective contract gains the explicit amendment identity described below. The live store and replay must independently require the reservation to be within the applicable bound, rather than trusting a serialized total.

The result reference must designate the one exact `${recordKey}-result.json` produced for the owned record, with the ordinary `observation` role and full original length/hash. Enforce this identity at writing and outer acceptance. An arbitrary `observation`, `.json`, copied runtime file, alternate result name or second result does not acquire the larger cap. Current production already uses that exact path; source fixtures that use `local-result.json` must migrate to the real identity. Keep receipt/collector/inventory joins exact.

| Consumer/interface | Current behavior | Proposed change / obligation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `event-marker-program-acquire.mjs:42`, `createInvocationStore.writeProgramOuter` | Serializes the complete replayed local object, debits held reservation, writes an observation; receipt contains its exact ref. | Preserve JSON bytes and interface. Writer validates the exact result name and privately selected scope, enforces 262,144 only there, and debits actual bytes. No publication after cancellation or failed retention. |
| `validateProgramDependencies`, `reserveProgramOuter`, `programBudget`, G12 | Plan reservation at most 196,608; reservation is held before local positive; whole-invocation totals include it. | Selected PROGRAM maximum 458,752. Keep the existing budget fields and reservation timing. Store/G12/replay independently check the selected bound and unchanged normal/aggregate arithmetic. |
| `codec-record.mjs`, `retainProgramReplay` | In-memory result enters private local replay; the historical `resolveOriginal` owner uses `readFile`. Replay manifest is a separate observation at most 196,608. | No representation change; manifest cap stays 196,608 and reflects the actual combined reservation. Adapt the owned `resolveOriginal` read to existing `readBounded`, checking the declared reference before fetch and enforcing the applicable existing role bound, deadline and cancellation during the read. |
| `replayProgramRecording(serialized, options)`, `readDirect` and new raw-result loader | Replay receives a parsed object and reconstructs proof/clock/classification; historical `readDirect` copies the resolver return before checking its actual length. No production raw-result file loader already exists. | Keep private proof construction. Before resolution reject an invalid or over-cap reference; the owned read uses existing `readBounded`. Check returned byte type and actual length before any copy or parse, then exact length/hash/EOF. The raw-result hard intake maximum is 262,144; private replay must still derive the applicable 196,608/262,144 scope limit. Direct object callers get the same serialized-size and derived scope gates. Parsing creates no certificate. |
| `verifyNativeOuterJoins`, `readRef/get` | PROGRAM result read has 196,608 cap. Each resolved ordinary outer original is held in an ID Map and contributes its actual length; PROGRAM has no native132 archive exemptions. | Only the exact result read may use 262,144 after scope/identity checks. Check declared and actual lengths before `Buffer.from`/parse; retain full equality, hash and EOF obligations. Compute `resultCharge` from that one proven original; require `charge - resultCharge <= 196608`, `charge <= reservedOuterBytes <= 458752`, and existing invocation limits. All other ordinary entries, including duplicate result copies under other IDs, remain in `charge`. |
| Non-`get` `rootLedger.lookup` A reader | The historical controller parses the returned `original` directly. A is an ordinary charged outer original, not a Root-only source/review audit body. | The lookup owner enforces a 196,608-byte maximum with existing bounded-read machinery before returning the body. Check any declared reference before body fetch and returned byte type/actual length before copying or `JSON.parse`; preserve whole-original identity/hash/EOF and ledger joins. Include all A bytes in O and the combined reservation; no new allowance. |
| PROGRAM collector and `inventoryArtifacts` | Receipt/terminal each 65,536; at most 256 payload files; generic transport file bound 64 MiB; complete hash inventory. | No larger cap needed. They carry opaque result bytes and references, not a new result format. Result semantic acceptance stays in the exact scoped writer/reader. |
| Root Python retrieval and Node wrapper | Generic original objects at most 64 MiB; two complete remote reads, one local retained copy; helper input/output/receipt each 196,608. | No cap changes. The result is an ordinary listed object; the envelope contains inventory references, not its full body. Result loading for replay must use the bounded raw parser, rather than unbounded `readFile` followed by `JSON.parse`. |
| `results.mjs`, mass/bridge observation writers | Qualification observation gzip cap 262,144 with 8 MiB inflation; result shards 262,144; nonliteral union requires a real independently accepted replay handle. | No changes to these caps or proof requirements. These distinct gzip/shard interfaces do not select the new raw PROGRAM allowance. Their current JSON field consumers need no format migration under A. |
| Source fixtures and full-canary regression | Small fixtures can fit; immutable full 64-episode result intentionally demonstrates the two result-bound failures. | Exercise the actual writer, bounded loader, independent replay and simulated outer path with the unchanged complete canary. A storage-bound test is not media acceptance. Preserve independent evidence/clock/outer guards and all existing negative cases. |

The raw parser's maximum is an input-allocation guard; it does not grant the R94 scope. Apply this intake order to controller `get/readRef`, `program-replay.readDirect`, the new raw-result loader, and the non-`get` A lookup boundary:

1. Validate the declared complete reference, including identity, positive safe length and hash, against its applicable bound **before resolution/body fetch**. Keep stricter existing per-role bounds; the 262,144 result allowance applies only to the exact result. Where A's lookup owns its reference metadata, that owner checks it before reading the body; a supplied candidate key or absence of caller-visible metadata cannot remove the fixed 196,608 intake maximum.
2. The owner of each actual file read must enforce the applicable bound during acquisition using existing `readBounded`, together with existing deadline, cancellation, file-identity and ownership rules. `codec-record` owns its `resolveOriginal` adapter and must replace its unbounded `readFile` acquisition there. `readDirect` and the raw-result loader require this bounded resolver contract. The Root-owned `rootLedger.lookup` implementation/adapter likewise owns bounded acquisition of A. No new general reader framework, helper cap or filesystem-access allowance is introduced.
3. On return, validate the byte type and actual length **before** `Buffer.from`, an equivalent copy, string conversion or `JSON.parse`. Reject a declared-small/returned-oversized value and any actual-length mismatch before those stages, even if its declared size looked admissible. Preserve exact original length/hash, full EOF and identity checks before accepting or parsing the original.
4. A's complete positive original is at most 196,608 and remains fully charged in O. Its ledger/candidate/approval joins are still mandatory. Root-only audit-role treatment never applies to A, and remaining room in the combined reservation cannot enlarge A or any other stricter role bound.

The historical `get` and `readDirect` copy-before-length-check ordering must be corrected at those exact boundaries. A resolver receiving an already oversized fake buffer cannot undo its caller's allocation; it must reject before making another copy or parsing it. Do not claim an already-parsed arbitrary object was bounded before its caller parsed it. No old unbounded raw-result production loader exists to declare migrated: add and wire the small adapter explicitly through the real readers and source fixtures.

## Effective contract and complete authority originals

**R94 is an intentional contract amendment; R93 is a behavior-preserving DATA refactor.** They must have separate review dispositions. R85's original design paragraph 77 preserves the older numeric bounds, and its G12 row says to parse/serialize/replay the complete ledger "under the unchanged limits." R90 already supplies an explicit subsequent numeric amendment. Neither those words nor R93's source-only relocation authorize this new result/reservation bound.

The accepted R85/R93 baseline `PROGRAM_SOURCE_CONTRACT` has three fixed hashes, compared exactly by `validateProgramDependencies`, `makeNativeCandidate`, launch preparation and common outer replay. `requiredAuthorityReferences` gathers every `proof.descriptions[].auditRef/sourceRefs` and `requireAuthorityMembership` joins those references to full K audit originals. The outer checker actually reopens/hashes every K source/audit original and A binds the exact K/audit set. However, **putting a new document somewhere in K.auditRefs alone does not make it a required R94 premise**: no current check requires that particular amendment identity.

Use a concrete additive effective-contract identity, not a replacement for the native-source proof. After R93 has preserved the original three values in `scripts/event-marker-program-contract.mjs`, R94 intentionally adds one fixed `resultSizing` field naming the SHA-256 of **this complete final body once frozen, peer-dispositioned and adopted by Root**. Its required audit ID is exactly `program-result-sizing-r94-v1`. Keep these R85 base values byte-for-byte:

| Base field | Exact original SHA-256 |
| --- | --- |
| `design` | `aa6d1308c3ed17a2440004d06ef85a5d47aa47d09034b11fe8ddc01087f13c93` |
| `guards` | `a9cdeede2f5be1c9daf79cc9842b60e079e1bc2dff8501b3cc9cf75f4f9073f7` |
| `pins` | `8cd6382c44b4c70bde56a20387d8268b8133023c79bd8c5afd90027dbd00e75a` |

The full four-field object is a **new effective contract**, still compared exactly through the existing machinery. G0 and G12 descriptions must each include a full-original AuditRef with the exact ID `program-result-sizing-r94-v1`, actual complete frozen-body length and SHA matching `resultSizing`; the fixed validator must require that reference, rather than merely accepting arbitrary nonempty sourceRefs. Ranges may cite passages but cannot substitute for the complete amendment body. Full R85/native-pins originals remain required by the existing reviewed closure; the amendment explicitly changes only the two result/reservation bounds and their scoped accounting/reader checks. G1–G11/native argv, source constructions and clock/conservation algorithms remain their original obligations.

The final design, original design review, this final amendment and its exact-body peer disposition, Root's R94 disposition and subsequent exact implementation/semantic review must remain complete resolvable originals in the established Root authority/source store, with required refs in proof/catalog/K and the real A's matching audit set. Complete authority possession is required even where the audit body is outside the runtime-use ledger.

Genuine Root-only audit/source/review originals remain AuditRefs under R76 S1/S2. Root must possess, reopen and verify their complete bodies and account for their actual Root storage and read work. Those audit-only bodies are outside the per-record runtime-use numeric ledger; this is the existing audit role, not an R87 code-body discount. The contract DATA leaf, runtime descriptions, references, acquisition/recheck observations and every body actually loaded or used as runtime DATA retain their full existing numeric/aggregate charges and logical-use multiplicity. Additional physical copies retain their actual storage charges. R94 creates no new body charge, role exemption or deduplication rule.

Apply those existing roles to each actual acquisition/use: do not add genuine Root-only audit bodies to N/G/O merely because they are required authority, and do not move a loaded runtime body into the audit role to reduce N/G/O. Recompute the actual charged runtime inputs/uses, code/DATA source sets, Root audit storage/read work and all retained copies under their applicable existing budgets. This amendment's own SHA and byte length are deliberately not written into its body. Freeze and hash the body, obtain the original peer's disposition naming those exact bytes, and then obtain Root's R94 adoption before embedding its hash in source DATA. Later implementation review belongs in the externally built source/audit catalog, not back inside the source it reviews.

The acyclic order is: immutable base/native-source originals → final reviewed result-sizing amendment and design peer → explicit R94 → contract DATA and implementation → full exact-source/semantic review and runtime descriptions/catalog → source/image correspondence and K → external A → I/C/Q → observed L. No future K/A/I/L hash, promised successful run, or placeholder approval enters the earlier amendment or DATA leaf. A separate complete policy/audit document could technically suffice **if** its identity were obligatorily checked through this same chain; the additive contract field makes that requirement explicit and prevents an optional audit attachment from masquerading as authority.

The DATA-separation plan must still pass its unchanged-three-hash requirement at its own R93 boundary. R94's later fourth field is an enumerated, reviewed change, not evidence that R93 preserved the final combined contract unchanged. The accepted design baseline has no such field; no current or later writer may enable the proposed larger bound before this exact amendment is adopted. For sources built after R94, native132 and other non-PROGRAM domains may see the new shared contract identity but retain every old domain cap; the amendment grants them no larger result or reservation allowance.

| Selected PROGRAM other chargeable outer originals | Within the shared 196,608 | **196,608 independently enforced** |
| Other scopes' result/reservation limits | Existing 196,608 | Unchanged |

| PROGRAM replay manifest; K/I/Q/L/readback/helper documents | Their existing 196,608 bounds; C also 4,096 | Unchanged |

| PROGRAM receipt / collector terminal | 65,536 each | Unchanged |

All existing capture/channel, stderr/argv, source/sample/row, image 2 GiB, context/override, cancellation, EOF, ownership and absolute-deadline gates remain. No global replacement of `196608` is appropriate.

## Accounting, retained copies and memory

The replay manifest snapshots its budget **before** its own write and before the result/receipt. Let `N` and `G` be that snapshot's numeric and aggregate amounts; `M` the manifest's actual bytes; `R` the exact result original; and `O` every other chargeable outer original, including A, receipt, K/I/C/Q/L/image, metadata, collector terminal, retrieval input/completion/readback and required runtime readbacks. Preserve the actual identity-based ordinary charges:

`R <= 262144; O <= 196608; R + O <= declared combined reservation <= 458752`

`N + M + R + O <= 1572864`

`G + M + R + O <= invocation aggregate - 65536`

G includes the full per-invocation R87 code union; N/G already include all ordinary DATA and distinct E/D logical uses. No new code/DATA eligibility follows from R94. The group independently counts its full physical storage and finite resolver. The separate R93 eligibility/refactor work can alter both N and G and must be incorporated before any real fit claim. Genuine Root-only audit/source/review bodies are not added to N/G/O; their complete possession, Root storage and read work remain required under R76 S1/S2.

| Existing role or actual event | Numeric / aggregate accounting | Retained-copy and read-work obligations |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Scoped result R and ordinary outer originals O, **including A** | Full existing numeric/aggregate charge. R is added once from the pre-result snapshot; every other actually charged identity/use stays in O. | Retain full matching originals. Additional physical copies count their storage; a result copy under another charged ID remains in O even if byte-identical. |
| Contract DATA leaf, loaded runtime DATA, plans, runtime descriptions, catalogs, refs and acquisition/recheck observations | Full existing numeric/aggregate charges and logical-use multiplicity, including distinct E/D uses and every actual observation event. | Full actual retained storage and actual reads/rechecks remain counted. Root already possessing a copy does not exempt runtime loading/use of that body. |
| Independently approved R87 implementation bodies | Only the existing approved code-body numeric exception; full unique code union in G per using invocation. References and actual acquisition/recheck observations retain ordinary charges. | Full actual group storage and finite resolver; actual extra copies count storage. Each using invocation reserves its own full union before use. |
| **Genuine Root-only AuditRefs**: source, policy, design and review bodies under R76 S1/S2 | Audit-only bodies stay outside the per-record runtime-use N/G/O ledger. Their runtime descriptions and references remain charged. This is not an R87 exception and cannot be selected for a runtime body. | Root possesses, reopens and verifies every complete body. Count all actual Root audit storage, extra physical copies and actual read/hash work under existing storage/work limits. |
| Additional retained copies and repeated actual uses/reads | Apply each original's existing role and ordinary logical-use rules; no equal-hash discount or new per-copy numeric rule. | Count actual retained storage and read/hash work. Reusing a cached Map entry performs no fresh resolver read; any real new acquisition/use must remain visible. |
| Transient buffers/parsed graphs and Root's two streaming remote passes | A numeric ledger is not RSS; two reads do not invent a second retained original. No existing evidence-body/use charge is erased. | Measure actual transient memory and both complete remote read/hash passes. The second streaming pass creates no second full local file; all files and buffers that actually are retained still count. |

The live store holds the reservation before result creation, converts `R` of that hold into an ordinary retained observation, and keeps the residual held through receipt finalization. Independent replay starts from the earlier manifest and adds `M`, then the outer Map adds `R + O`. Those are two validations of the same final ledger: do not subtract the result because the producer wrote it, and do not accidentally add it twice to the *same pre-result snapshot*. Reject a forged/resized reservation or omitted result charge. Any separately retained/copied/used original receives its existing ordinary charge; equal hashes do not waive it. Reusing the already acquired Map entry performs no fresh resolver read. A second identity that actually resolves another copy remains charged, even if the body is identical.

Storage and read-work are also concrete, separate quantities; a numeric ledger is not a process-RSS measurement:

| Actual stage | Result contribution for this witness | At the proposed maximum |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| One retained result original in a store | 231,064 B | 262,144 B |
| Two retained full copies, if both exist | 462,128 B | 524,288 B |
| Root's mandatory two remote read/hash passes | 462,128 B of read work; one 231,064 B local copy | 524,288 B of read work; one 262,144 B local copy |
| Three simultaneous full byte buffers | 693,192 B | 786,432 B |

Producer serialization holds a JSON string and UTF-8 buffer beside the existing object graph; filesystem digest and collector upload read the original again. Root retrieval uses chunks at most 65,536 and does not retain its second remote pass. The outer resolver may hold its returned buffer while `get` makes a full copy; byte equality additionally constructs another full result buffer, and JSON parsing/stringification and replay objects consume heap. Three buffers plus a two-byte-per-character JSON string alone can account for about **1,155,320 witness bytes / 1,310,720 maximum bytes**, excluding the source/parsed graphs, V8 overhead, ropes/copies, replay's retained channel originals and kernel cache. This is a component arithmetic example, **not an RSS upper bound**. Actual peak RSS and read/hash elapsed work are unknown and must be measured in the connected path. New retained duplicate files or repeated actual read/use events cannot be hidden behind this example or the result reference.

The source-only checkpoint30 `green-all-marker-capacity-source.log` (400,212 bytes, SHA-256 `7930dad0e4fc90c8ea4472d9cd9cf90de54d66ed83c621363a78e11ded77a951`) reports a prior SIMULATED unchanged-canary budget of `N=565744`, `G=11421563`, code originals 459,687, and old reservation 196,608. The immutable result names a 13,881-byte replay manifest. **These are not a joined final-witness ledger and the old code eligibility is not current approval.** Only as sensitivity arithmetic, substituting those N/G/M values gives:

| Illustration, not fit evidence | Numeric | Aggregate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Witness R + full 196,608 other-outer allowance | 1,007,297 | 11,863,116 |
| Full 458,752 combined reservation | 1,038,377 | 11,894,196 |
| Headroom for the latter below unchanged normal limits | 534,487 | 4,817,484 |

Actual group storage additionally includes the registered full code/source resolver, outer artifacts and any other retained copies. It cannot be equated with the illustrative invocation total. Reopen and measure the exact final manifest, full actual outer ledger and storage layout before claiming these inequalities hold.

## Remaining unknowns and bounded rejection

The 31,080-byte witness margin is not a population proof. Existing semantic limits admit much larger shapes: 4,096 fixed 185-byte episode leaves alone would occupy **1,028,097 JSON bytes** as Base64 strings; full episode objects are larger. Metadata, detector blocks, decimal widths, assurance/projection size and actual native observations also affect JSON length. Existing sample/channel/row limits are separate from serialized-result fit. Keep them, measure actual serialization, and fail closed above the result maximum; no automatic enlargement, smaller train, missing facts or fixture-only alternate policy.

Exactly unresolved before a fit/acceptance claim:

- The complete result for the final repaired source and approved physical CODE/DATA layout, together with its **same-run** replay manifest and every logical use. The immutable witness proves size only for its own bytes.
- Actual `O`, especially Root helper/input/readback and image/native metadata documents. 196,608 is a proposed retained bound for O, not a measured full-canary total. The corresponding reviewed plan must reserve enough `R + O`; even 458,752 can fail if O exceeds its own bound.
- Actual retained-copy topology, final invocation/group storage, peak JS/Python RSS, read/hash work, free-space high-water and elapsed work under existing deadlines. No runtime measurements were made here.
- Whether every admitted future 64-episode/native shape fits 262,144. No such guarantee is available. Larger semantic populations remain subject to the hard result gate.
- The final connected source regression and independent review. There is no actual A/image/native/media/outer acceptance from this design or the SIMULATED source path.

## Focused implementation and review plan

After the original peer dispositions this exact frozen final body and Root adopts it in R94, Root amends the existing writing plan and dispatches this finite set through the sole implementation writer after the separate R93 task review:

1. `scripts/event-marker-evidence-policy.mjs`: fixed PROGRAM result/other-outer/combined limits and existing authenticated-scope derivation. `scripts/event-marker-program-contract.mjs` after the separate R93 refactor: the additive immutable amendment identity in its fully charged DATA body. `scripts/event-marker-program-guards.mjs`: scope-derived plan-reservation bound and mandatory G0/G12 amendment-reference checks. No numeric-policy ID/value change. Keep `event-marker-authority-closure.mjs`'s existing full reference-membership traversal; it needs no new registry or broad relaxation.
2. `scripts/marker-qualification/artifacts.mjs`: exact result identity, privately selected cap, bounded reservation and unchanged transactional debit/restore/final checks. `scripts/event-marker-conservation.mjs` G12: verify the applicable reservation ceiling as well as normal/aggregate arithmetic.
3. `scripts/marker-qualification/codec-record.mjs`: the small bounded-read adaptation of its existing `resolveOriginal` ownership, using existing `readBounded` with the applicable role bound and acquisition control. `scripts/marker-qualification/program-replay.mjs`: declared-reference checks before resolution; returned byte-type/actual-length checks before copies in `readDirect`; new bounded raw-result intake with the same ordering; applicable result/reservation checks; complete original replay unchanged. `scripts/event-marker-native-controller.mjs`: exact larger result read; declared-reference and returned-type/length checks before copy/parse in `get/readRef` and the non-`get` A path; bound the Root-owned `rootLedger.lookup` acquisition/adapter to 196,608 using existing bounded-read ownership; independently derive reservation and non-result outer charge. Preserve exact length/hash/EOF and all stricter per-role bounds. Use the existing modules and read primitive; no new registry, loader framework or generic serializer.
4. `tests/fixtures/marker-positive-program.mjs`, `tests/scripts/event-marker-positive-program.test.mjs`, `event-marker-positive-program-fix1.test.mjs`, `event-marker-positive-program-fix2.test.mjs`: select the reviewed reservation only in the proper simulated scope, migrate the result name/loader, add connected accounting/boundary regressions. Preserve old legacy/native132 cases. The exact plan DATA, candidate/source inventories and implementation report must be refreshed by the established existing process after these source bytes settle. Source pins are reviewed identities, not values to update mechanically to evade a check.

The acquisition CLI, collector, Root retrieval Python/Node helper, Engine parser, qualification JSON consumers and wire layouts require **no cap or format change** for A. If implementation discovers an additional unavoidable cap change there, return that concrete finding instead of silently expanding R94.

Required meaningful source-only checks:

- Real result write/load at 262,144 and rejection at 262,145, including LF and UTF-8 byte lengths; old 196,608/+1 boundaries under legacy/sourceClosed/unselected/native132. Distinguish structural storage success from semantic acceptance.
- Other-outer 196,608/+1 and combined 458,752/+1; unchanged R90 normal/final/reserve and normal aggregate boundaries. Verify result is charged, a distinct second copied original is charged, exhausted normal fails despite unused failure reserve, and mismatched reservation/manifest totals fail.
- Wrong role/name/record/invocation/domain/producer/retrieval, forged/missing/stale private selection, altered plan policy, and runtime/bootstrap/profile/source/native receipt bytes under the unchanged caps. A same-byte runtime original relabeled as a result must not obtain the allowance.
- Missing/wrong/stale `resultSizing` identity, wrong `program-result-sizing-r94-v1` audit ID, absent G0/G12 amendment ref, missing or changed complete policy/review original, an audit attached only as an optional K extra, and mismatched K/A/proof contract must fail. Retain exact original R85 base hashes, native source pins and native argv equality. No source ref to a future K/A/I may satisfy the amendment.
- C2 reader falsifications at `codec-record.resolveOriginal`, `readDirect`, the new raw-result loader and controller/A boundaries: an invalid or over-cap declared reference must reject before body fetch; a declared-small/returned-oversized result or original must reject before copy/string conversion/parse; wrong returned type and exact-length mismatch must likewise reject before those stages. An A body of 196,609 bytes must reject before copy/`JSON.parse`, even with spare combined reservation; verify bounded owned acquisition and A's full ordinary O charge. Retain exact length/hash/EOF, cancellation and stricter role-bound negatives.
- Missing/extra/changed episode, prelude, guard, raw endpoint, residual-total, clock, assurance, projection or observation facts still fail independent replay or exact-original joining. Retain original-hash, length, truncation, EOF, inventory, wrong-copy and full original-possession negatives.
- Cancellation while result write/digest/read/receipt finalization is pending: no late positive commit, reservation cannot be spent twice, primary failure survives failed retention, and actual owned cleanup remains required.
- Real source APIs from unchanged request **49,869 / `295c03033e1f6f31a14538a0e84622485b9fb74a92665f7ffbeed1cd1065ea6d`** and construction **49,722 / `4eed2237ca4ddbecb43c0a417e042997607bdff0493efa28150cd111adfe3fa1`**, through full 64-episode private replay, result retention, bounded loading, complete simulated outer joins and accepted-handle union checks. Record exact result bytes, every original/use, N/G/M/R/O, retained copies and reservation arithmetic. Use SIMULATED native/authority boundaries explicitly; do not fabricate proof brands or run native/media operations for this source check.

Existing result JSON has no format migration under A. Historical originals remain replayable with their original reviewed source/contract; the new effective-contract checker must not silently accept a stale three-field contract as R94 authority. An old reader correctly rejects a new larger result. New source/plan/contract/candidate identities require the existing coordinated review; a source-only R94 does not confer actual approval. All **79,996 IDs, 83 groups, 294 invocations, native132 commands/assertions, exact train and strong false flags** remain unchanged.
